title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms — PV, ET, PMF
subtitle: Philadelphia-negative MPNs driven by constitutive JAK-STAT activation (JAK2 V617F, CALR, MPL) · shared risks are thrombosis, progression to myelofibrosis, and blast-phase transformation
source: No Stanford handbook chapter — compiled from WHO 2022 / ICC criteria, NCCN MPN guidelines, and landmark trials. Verify against primary sources before acting.

blocks.heading: Driver mutations
blocks.footnote: PV is essentially always JAK2-mutated — a JAK2-negative erythrocytosis should send you back to the differential, not to a PV diagnosis. In ET, CALR predicts higher platelets but lower thrombosis risk than JAK2.

blocks.heading: Mutation biology
items: All three drivers converge on JAK-STAT — JAK inhibitors work irrespective of which one is present

JAK2 V617F — exon 14 pseudokinase (JH2) domain; relieves autoinhibition → ligand-independent signaling. Homozygosity via 9p uniparental disomy is common in PV/PMF, rare in ET; higher allele burden tracks with PV phenotype, pruritus and fibrotic progression
JAK2 exon 12 — ~3% of PV: isolated erythrocytosis, younger, very low EPO; outcomes similar to V617F

CALR — exon 9 frameshift; the mutant C-terminus loses the KDEL ER-retention motif and instead activates MPL — which is exactly why CALR occurs in ET and PMF but never in PV. Type 1 (del52) predominates in PMF and is favorable; type 2 (ins5) in ET
MPL W515L/K — exon 10 TPO receptor; ET and PMF only. Triple-negative — worst prognosis in PMF

blocks.heading: Diagnostic anchors (WHO 2022)
items: PV: Hb >16.5 (M) / >16.0 (F) or Hct >49% (M) / >48% (F) + trilineage hypercellularity with pleomorphic megakaryocytes + JAK2 mutation; subnormal EPO is a minor criterion
ET: platelets ≥450 ×109/L + large hyperlobulated (“staghorn”) megakaryocytes + reticulin ≤ grade 1 + a clonal marker, having excluded other MPNs
PMF: megakaryocyte atypia with dense clustering + fibrosis grade (prefibrotic vs overt) + leukoerythroblastosis, anemia, splenomegaly, ↑LDH

blocks.html:
The hardest and highest-stakes distinction is prefibrotic PMF vs ET. They look alike on counts, but prefibrotic PMF has materially worse survival and higher transformation risk. It turns on marrow morphology — megakaryocyte clustering and atypia — not on the CBC.

Masked PV: concurrent iron deficiency can normalize the hematocrit. If JAK2 is mutated with a “normal” Hct, think PV.

Splanchnic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari, portal vein) — test JAK2 in everyone, even with normal counts; MPN is a leading occult cause.

boxes: do not replace iron — it defeats the target
High risk — age ≥60 or prior thrombosis
aspirin 81 mg — consider BID if JAK2+ or CV RFs
observation reasonable if very low risk
High risk — prior thrombosis, or >60 + JAK2+
refer intermediate-2 / high risk if eligible

blocks.heading: Risk stratification
rows: High risk = age ≥60 OR prior thrombosis; low risk = neither. High risk (or symptomatic/progressive) triggers cytoreduction

IPSET-thrombosis (revised): very low = ≤60, no thrombosis, JAK2 WT · low = ≤60, no thrombosis, JAK2-mutant · intermediate = >60, no thrombosis, JAK2 WT · high = prior thrombosis, or >60 AND JAK2-mutant
IPSS (at diagnosis) · DIPSS / DIPSS-plus (any time) · MIPSS70 / MIPSS70+ v2 (molecular; transplant candidates) · GIPSS (genetic only)
blocks.footnote: Non-driver mutations set prognosis, not diagnosis. High-molecular-risk in PMF: ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2, U2AF1 Q157 — these drive the MIPSS scores and push toward transplant. TP53 drives blast-phase transformation.

blocks.heading: Agents & dosing
rows: 81 mg daily; BID if JAK2+ or high-risk ET
100 µg SQ q2wk (50 if switching from HU); titrate by 50 to max 500
PV 10 mg BID · MF 5–20 mg BID by platelet count
blocks.footnote: Fedratinib requires thiamine — check and replete before and during treatment (Wernicke encephalopathy). Never stop ruxolitinib abruptly — cytokine rebound/withdrawal syndrome; taper.

blocks.heading: Complications & pearls
items: Acquired von Willebrand syndrome with extreme thrombocytosis (>1000–1500) — paradoxical bleeding. Check ristocetin cofactor before starting aspirin; hold aspirin if severely reduced
CYTO-PV: Hct target <45% gave ~4× fewer cardiovascular deaths and major thromboses than a 45–50% target — the number to defend
Post-PV / post-ET myelofibrosis (IWG-MRT criteria) — suspect with rising LDH, falling counts, enlarging spleen, new constitutional symptoms
Blast phase (≥20% blasts) is dismal and chemo-refractory — allogeneic transplant is the only meaningful option
Aquagenic pruritus in PV — antihistamines, SSRIs, interferon, or ruxolitinib (a genuine quality-of-life issue, not a nuisance)
Anemia in MF: ESAs if EPO <500, danazol, luspatercept, or switch to momelotinib
